claim: It divides north-east from south-west Sydney, running from the airport through Parramatta
test: share of suburbs whose café side matches the north-east side of an airport-Parramatta line, vs random Sydneys

claim: The Latte Line is a figure of speech, not something in the coffee data
test: the Latte Line's own test: cafés vs fast-food places per suburb, against random Sydneys (Section 9)
figure: real pattern (p = 0.002 for any geography); border cleaner than random Sydneys on its own (p = 0.02), not after allowing for 6 food lines (0.12)

claim: The Red Rooster Line marks where Red Rooster restaurants stop
test: Red Rooster vs the nearest other chicken chain, against random store layouts
figure: cleaner than chance on its own (p = 0.03), not after correction (0.16)

claim: The line divides the haves from the have-nots
test: Money Lines (rent, mortgage, household income): is money a line, and whose route does it follow?
figure: rent: p = 0.14, matches Latte 69%, Hi-Vis 76%; mortgage: p = 0.15, matches Latte 72%, Hi-Vis 79%; household income: p = 0.22, matches Latte 66%, Hi-Vis 75%
verdict: slope, not a line; follows work more than coffee

claim: Homes above the line are almost always worth over $1m, below it under
test: mortgage repayments (2021 Census; sale prices are not in the census): above-median share on each side
figure: café side 70% above the city median; fast-food side 79% below

claim: School results depend on which side of the line you live
test: university-degree share (HSC and NAPLAN are not in the census): match with the café side, vs random Sydneys

claim: The 2021 lockdown 'LGAs of concern' were the Latte Line's other side
test: councils of concern (approximated by ABS SA3 regions) vs the fast-food side, balanced accuracy, vs random Sydneys
figure: 79% of their residents on the fast-food side; balanced accuracy 81% (random Sydneys 50%); Hi-Vis (work) 83%, rent 78%, income 77%; without Penrith 81%

test: how much cleaner than random the Hi-Vis border is in each census, 2001-2021 (the venue data has no history)
figure: z = -2.8 (2001), -3.1 (2006), -3.4 (2011), -3.1 (2016), -3.0 (2021): a real line in every census, no steady hardening

claim: The line is breaking down as western chicken chains spread east
test: the Charcoal Chook Line (charcoal-chicken shops vs other takeaways)

claim: Melbourne's divide is much weaker than Sydney's, with no clear boundary
test: real lines in each city under the same test
